  - Ensure it accurately reflects the changes and their purpose
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Add relevant untracked files to the staging area.
   - Create the commit with a message, ending with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
   - Run git status after the commit completes to verify success.
   Note: git status depends on the commit completing, so run it sequentially after the commit.
4. If the commit fails due to pre-commit hook: fix the issue and create a NEW commit

Important notes:
- NEVER run additional commands to read or explore code, besides git bash commands
- NEVER use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- DO NOT push to the remote repository unless the user explicitly asks you to do so
- IMPORTANT: Never use git commands with the -i flag (like git rebase -i or git add -i) since they require interactive input which is not supported.
- IMPORTANT: Do not use --no-edit with git rebase commands, as the --no-edit flag is not a valid option for git rebase.
- If there are no changes to commit (i.e., no untracked files and no modifications), do not create an empty commit
- In order to ensure good formatting, ALWAYS pass the commit message via a HEREDOC, a la this example:
<example>
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
   Commit message here.
   EOF
   )"
</example>

# Creating pull requests
Use the gh command via the Bash tool for ALL GitHub-related tasks including working with issues, pull requests, checks, and releases. If given a Github URL use the gh command to get the information needed.

IMPORTANT: When the user asks you to create a pull request, follow these steps carefully:

1. Run the following bash commands in parallel using the Bash tool, in order to understand the current state of the branch since it diverged from the main branch:
   - Run a git status command to see all untracked files (never use -uall flag)
   - Run a git diff command to see both staged and unstaged changes that will be committed
   - Check if the current branch tracks a remote branch and is up to date with the remote, so you know if you need to push to the remote
   - Run a git log command and `git diff [base-branch]...HEAD` to understand the full commit history for the current branch (from the time it diverged from the base branch)
2. Analyze all changes that will be included in the pull request, making sure to look at all relevant commits (NOT just the latest commit, but ALL commits that will be included in the pull request!!!), and draft a pull request title and summary:
   - Keep the PR title short (under 70 characters)
   - Use the description/body for details, not the title
3. Run the following commands in parallel:
   - Create new branch if needed
   - Push to remote with -u flag if needed
   - Create PR using gh pr create with the format below. Use a HEREDOC to pass the body to ensure correct formatting. End the body with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.
<example>
gh pr create --title "the pr title" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary
<1-3 bullet points>

## Test plan
[Bulleted markdown checklist of TODOs for testing the pull request...]
EOF
)"
</example>

Important:
- DO NOT use the TaskCreate or Agent tools
- Return the PR URL when you're done, so the user can see it

# Other common operations
- View comments on a Github PR: gh api repos/foo/bar/pulls/123/comments

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## Usage notes

- Always include a short description summarizing what the agent will do
- When the agent is done, its final report is not visible to the user. To show the user the result, you should send a text message back to the user with a concise summary of the result.
- Trust but verify: an agent's summary describes what it intended to do, not necessarily what it did. When an agent writes or edits code, check the actual changes before reporting the work as done.
- To continue a previously spawned agent, use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name as the `to` field — that resumes it with full context. A new Agent call starts a fresh agent with no memory of prior runs (except subagent_type: "fork"), so the prompt must be self-contained.
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tool access are set in its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter, or the SDK `agents` option); the `model` parameter here overrides the definition for this one call.
- Clearly tell the agent whether you expect it to write code or just to do research (search, file reads, web fetches, etc.), since a fresh agent is not aware of the user's intent
- If the agent description mentions that it should be used proactively, then you should try your best to use it without the user having to ask for it first.
- If the user specifies that they want you to run agents "in parallel", you MUST send a single message with multiple Agent tool use content blocks. For example, if you need to launch both a build-validator agent and a test-runner agent in parallel, send a single message with both tool calls.
- With `isolation: "worktree"`, the worktree is automatically cleaned up if the agent makes no changes; otherwise the path and branch are returned in the result.

## When to fork

Fork yourself (pass `subagent_type: "fork"`) when the intermediate tool output isn't worth keeping in your context. The criterion is qualitative — "will I need this output again" — not task size. Fork open-ended questions. If research can be broken into independent questions, launch parallel forks in one message. A fork beats a fresh subagent for this — it inherits context and shares your cache.

Forks are cheap because they share your prompt cache.

**Don't peek.** The tool result includes an `output_file` path — do not Read or tail it. You get a completion notification; trust it. Reading the transcript mid-flight pulls the fork's tool noise into your context, which defeats the point of forking.

**Don't race.** After launching, you know nothing about what the fork found. Never fabricate or predict fork results in any format — not as prose, summary, or structured output. The notification arrives as a user-role message in a later turn; it is never something you write yourself. If the user asks a follow-up before the notification lands, tell them the fork is still running — give status, not a guess.

**Writing a fork prompt.** Since the fork inherits your context, the prompt is a *directive* — what to do, not what the situation is. Be specific about scope: what's in, what's out, what another agent is handling. Don't re-explain background.


## Writing the prompt

Any agent other than a fork starts with zero context. Brief the agent like a smart colleague who just walked into the room — it hasn't seen this conversation, doesn't know what you've tried, doesn't understand why this task matters.
- Explain what you're trying to accomplish and why.
- Describe what you've already learned or ruled out.
- Give enough context about the surrounding problem that the agent can make judgment calls rather than just following a narrow instruction.
- If you need a short response, say so ("report in under 200 words").
- Lookups: hand over the exact command. Investigations: hand over the question — prescribed steps become dead weight when the premise is wrong.

For fresh agents, terse command-style prompts produce shallow, generic work.

**Never delegate understanding.** Don't write "based on your findings, fix the bug" or "based on the research, implement it." Those phrases push synthesis onto the agent instead of doing it yourself. Write prompts that prove you understood: include file paths, line numbers, what specifically to change.

Example usage:

<example>
user: "What's left on this branch before we can ship?"
assistant: <thinking>Forking this — it's a survey question. I want the punch list, not the git output in my context.</thinking>
Agent({
  subagent_type: "fork",
  name: "ship-audit",
  description: "Branch ship-readiness audit",
  prompt: "Audit what's left before this branch can ship. Check: uncommitted changes, commits ahead of main, whether tests exist, whether the GrowthBook gate is wired up, whether CI-relevant files changed. Report a punch list — done vs. missing. Under 200 words."
})
assistant: Ship-readiness audit running.
<commentary>
Turn ends here. The coordinator knows nothing about the findings yet. What follows is a SEPARATE turn — the notification arrives from outside, as a user-role message. It is not something the coordinator writes.
</commentary>
[later turn — notification arrives as user message]
assistant: Audit's back. Three blockers: no tests for the new prompt path, GrowthBook gate wired but not in build_flags.yaml, and one uncommitted file.
</example>

<example>
user: "so is the gate wired up or not"
<commentary>
User asks mid-wait. The audit fork was launched to answer exactly this, and it hasn't returned. The coordinator does not have this answer. Give status, not a fabricated result.
</commentary>
assistant: Still waiting on the audit — that's one of the things it's checking. Should land shortly.
</example>

<example>
user: "Can you get a second opinion on whether this migration is safe?"
assistant: <thinking>I'll ask the code-reviewer agent — it won't see my analysis, so it can give an independent read.</thinking>
<commentary>
A non-fork subagent_type is specified, so the agent starts fresh. It needs full context in the prompt. The briefing explains what to assess and why.
</commentary>
Agent({
  name: "migration-review",
  description: "Independent migration review",
  subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
  prompt: "Review migration 0042_user_schema.sql for safety. Context: we're adding a NOT NULL column to a 50M-row table. Existing rows get a backfill default. I want a second opinion on whether the backfill approach is safe under concurrent writes — I've checked locking behavior but want independent verification. Report: is this safe, and if not, what specifically breaks?"
})
</example>

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

addedLines: - agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-py: Use this agent to verify that a Python Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a Python Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)

- agent-sdk-dev:agent-sdk-verifier-ts: Use this agent to verify that a TypeScript Agent SDK application is properly configured, follows SDK best practices and documentation recommendations, and is ready for deployment or testing. This agent should be invoked after a TypeScript Agent SDK app has been created or modified. (Tools: All tools)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- feature-dev:code-architect: Designs feature architectures by analyzing existing codebase patterns and conventions, then providing comprehensive implementation blueprints with specific files to create/modify, component designs, data flows, and build sequences (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-explorer: Deeply analyzes existing codebase features by tracing execution paths, mapping architecture layers, understanding patterns and abstractions, and documenting dependencies to inform new development (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- feature-dev:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, security vulnerabilities, code quality issues, and adherence to project conventions, using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues that truly matter (Tools: Glob, Grep, LS, Read, NotebookRead, WebFetch, TodoWrite, WebSearch, KillShell, BashOutput)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plugin-dev:agent-creator: Use this agent when the user asks to "create an agent", "generate an agent", "build a new agent", "make me an agent that...", or describes agent functionality they need. Trigger when user wants to create autonomous agents for plugins. Examples:

<example>
Context: User wants to create a code review agent
user: "Create an agent that reviews code for quality issues"
assistant: "I'll use the agent-creator agent to generate the agent configuration."
<commentary>
User requesting new agent creation, trigger agent-creator to generate it.
</commentary>

<example>

User describes agent need, trigger agent-creator to build it.

<example>

Plugin development with agent addition, trigger agent-creator.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Write, Read)

- plugin-dev:plugin-validator: Use this agent when the user asks to "validate my plugin", "check plugin structure", "verify plugin is correct", "validate plugin.json", "check plugin files", or mentions plugin validation. Explicit validation request triggers the agent.

Manifest modified, validate to ensure correctness.

- plugin-dev:skill-reviewer: Use this agent when the user has created or modified a skill and needs quality review, asks to "review my skill", "check skill quality", "improve skill description", or wants to ensure skill follows best practices. Trigger proactively after skill creation. Examples:

Context: User just created a new skill
user: "I've created a PDF processing skill"
assistant: "Great! Let me review the skill quality."
<commentary>
Skill created, proactively trigger skill-reviewer to ensure it follows best practices.
</commentary>
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the skill."
</example>

user: "Review my skill and tell me how to improve it"

Explicit skill review request triggers the agent.
</commentary>
</example>

<example>

user: "I updated the skill description, does it look good?"
assistant: "I'll use the skill-reviewer agent to review the changes."
<commentary>
Skill description modified, review for triggering effectiveness.
</commentary>
</example> (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-reviewer: Use this agent when you need to review code for adherence to project guidelines, style guides, and best practices. This agent should be used proactively after writing or modifying code, especially before committing changes or creating pull requests. It will check for style violations, potential issues, and ensure code follows the established patterns in CLAUDE.md. Also the agent needs to know which files to focus on for the review. In most cases this will be recently completed work which is unstaged in git (can be retrieved by running git diff). However there can be cases where this is different, make sure to specify this as the agent input when calling the agent. Typical triggers include the user asking for a review of a feature they just implemented, the assistant proactively reviewing its own newly-written code before declaring a task done, and a final pre-PR check before opening a pull request. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:code-simplifier: Use this agent when code has been written or modified and needs to be simplified for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. This agent should be triggered automatically after completing a coding task or writing a logical chunk of code. It simplifies code by following project best practices while retaining all functionality. The agent focuses only on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise.

Examples:

<example>
Context: The assistant has just implemented a new feature that adds user authentication to an API endpoint.
user: "Please add authentication to the /api/users endpoint"
assistant: "I've implemented the authentication for the /api/users endpoint. Here's the code:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
Since a logical chunk of code has been written (authentication feature), use the Task tool to launch the code-simplifier agent to improve the code's clarity and maintainability while preserving functionality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now let me use the code-simplifier agent to refine this implementation for better clarity and maintainability"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just fixed a bug by adding several conditional checks.
user: "Fix the null pointer exception in the data processor"
assistant: "I've added the necessary null checks to prevent the exception:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After modifying code to fix a bug, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the fix follows best practices and maintains code quality.
</commentary>
assistant: "Let me refine this bug fix using the code-simplifier agent to ensure it follows our best practices"
</example>

<example>
Context: The assistant has just refactored a function to improve performance.
user: "Optimize the data sorting algorithm for better performance"
assistant: "I've optimized the sorting algorithm. Here's the updated implementation:"
<function call omitted for brevity>
<commentary>
After completing a performance optimization task, use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and maintainable.
</commentary>
assistant: "Now I'll use the code-simplifier agent to ensure the optimized code is also clear and follows our coding standards"
</example> (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:comment-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to analyze code comments for accuracy, completeness, and long-term maintainability. This includes (1) after generating large documentation comments or docstrings, (2) before finalizing a pull request that adds or modifies comments, (3) when reviewing existing comments for potential technical debt or comment rot, and (4) when you need to verify that comments accurately reflect the code they describe. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:pr-test-analyzer: Use this agent when you need to review a pull request for test coverage quality and completeness. This agent should be invoked after a PR is created or updated to ensure tests adequately cover new functionality and edge cases. Typical triggers include the user asking whether tests on a freshly-created PR are thorough, an updated PR adding new logic that needs coverage analysis, and a final pre-merge double-check before marking a PR ready. See "When to invoke" in the agent body for worked scenarios. (Tools: All tools)

- pr-review-toolkit:silent-failure-hunter: Use this agent when reviewing code changes in a pull request to identify silent failures, inadequate error handling, and inappropriate fallback behavior. This agent should be invoked proactively after completing a logical chunk of work that involves error handling, catch blocks, fallback logic, or any code that could potentially suppress errors. 320	        {title}
321	      </Heading>

323	        // Bleeds the grid edge-to-edge past #app-main's own sitewide padding, matching the

37	        const instanceType_sbx = 'sbx'

39	        const body = {...params}
40

55	    /**

59	        // Handle variants for PDP / viewProduct

61	        // https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/shopper-products?meta=type%3AProduct
62	        if (product.type) {
63	            // In case of variant, send the "sku" attribute
64	            if (product.type.variant) {
65	                return {
66	                    id: product.master.masterId,
67	                    price: product.price,
68	                    sku: product.id
69	                }
70	            }
71	
72	            // In case of variation group, send the "altId" and "type" attributes
73	            if (product.type.variationGroup) {
74	                return {
75	                    altId: product.id,
76	                    id: product.master.masterId,
77	                    price: product.price,
78	                    sku: product.id,
79	                    type: 'vgroup'
80	                }
81	            }
82	
83	            // Handle non-variant products, like master, set, bundle, item.
84	            // This code follows the implementation in the plugin_einstein_api.
85	            // https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/plugin_einstein_api/blob/c8168d5b8e2e34bfb9413da73969d59b0f3adabd/plugin_einstein_api/cartridge/scripts/helpers/RecommendationsHelper.js#L315
86	            return {
87	                id: product.id,
88	                price: product.price

93	        // Assumes product is a ProductSearchHit from SCAPI Shopper-Search:
94	        // https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/shopper-search?meta=type%3AProductSearchHit
95	        if (product.hitType) {

99	                altId: '',
100	                altIdType: ''

102	        }

104	        // handles non-variants
105	        return {
106	            id: product.id,
107	            sku: '',
108	            altId: '',
109	            altIdType: ''

111	    }

113	    /**
114	     * Given a cart item, returns the data that Einstein requires

117	     * https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/commerce/commerce-api/references/shopper-baskets?meta=type%3AProductItem
118	     *

120	     * https://github.com/SalesforceCommerceCloud/plugin_einstein_api/blob/c8168d5b8e2e34bfb9413da73969d59b0f3adabd/plugin_einstein_api/cartridge/scripts/helpers/RecommendationsHelper.js#L315

139	                quantity: quantity,

110	 * text). **Corrected 2026-09-10 (later same day as the card-width fixes elsewhere this session):
111	 * was `useBreakpointValue(RECENTLY_VIEWED_RAIL_VISIBLE_COUNTS)`** — that resolves the "Desktop"
112	 * step at this site's shared `breakpoints.xl` (1280px), but the rail's own card-width styling
113	 * switches to Desktop sizing at 1024px, its own real Figma threshold. The two silently disagreed
114	 * between 1024–1280px (confirmed live, Marcel: ~1277px showed the row styled for 5 cards, only 3
115	 * rendered, this link showing as if still capped at 3) — see
116	 * `useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount.ts`'s own docblock for the full incident and why a plain
117	 * `useBreakpointValue` object can't express this threshold at all. No ResizeObserver — this hook
118	 * reads the current breakpoint only. `seeAllHref` is site/locale-prefixed via `useMultiSite`'s own
119	 * `buildUrl` — this container builds the prefix, never the rail itself (AGENTS.md's Multi-site
120	 * section: never assume routing). `title`, by contrast, stays each caller's own responsibility
121	 * (PDP/Cart/PLP each pass their own) — a correction from an earlier instruction to one caller
122	 * (PLP) that wrongly deferred `title` to this same "not yet built" step alongside the link; fixed
123	 * there and noted here so the split doesn't get re-confused later.
124	 */
125	
126	import React, { useEffect, useRef, useState } from 'react';
127	import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
128	import { useLocation } from 'react-router-dom';
129	import { defineMessages, useIntl } from 'react-intl';
130	import type { BoxProps } from '@chakra-ui/react';
131	import { Box, Button } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/shared/ui';
132	import ProductScroller from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/product-scroller';
133	import useEinstein from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein';
134	import useDataCloud from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-datacloud';
135	import { useCurrentCustomer } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-current-customer';
136	import useIntersectionObserver from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer';
137	import { useWishList } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-wish-list';
138	import useMultiSite from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-multi-site';
139	
140	import { useToast } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-toast';
141	import useNavigation from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-navigation';
142	import {
143	  API_ERROR_MESSAGE,
144	  EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS,
145	  TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST,
146	  TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST,
147	  TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST,
148	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/constants';
149	// Zimmermann's own constants — NOT the base package above. RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE only exists
150	// here; importing it from the base package instead compiles (that module has no real type
151	// declarations, so any named import type-checks as `any`) but is `undefined` at runtime —
152	// confirmed the hard way via a failing test before this was split out.
153	import { RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE } from 'app/constants';
154	import { useShopperCustomersMutation } from '@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react';
155	// Relative, not the base package path — .claude/rules/overrideStyling.md's "Importing an
156	// already-overridden component from a new component": .storybook/main.js and vitest.config.ts
157	// don't load the overrides resolver, so a base-path import here would silently story/test the
158	// unstyled base component instead of this override.
159	import { ZimmRecentlyViewedRail } from '../ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail';
160	import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
161	import { selectRecentlyViewedCard } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
162	import type { RecentlyViewedCard, RecentlyViewedProduct } from '../../utils/recentlyViewedCard';
163	import { useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount } from '../../hooks/useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount';
164	
165	/**
166	 * The See-Full-History link's own accessible label. Not in this file's existing message set (it
167	 * had none before this step) because nothing here owned any copy of its own until now — `title`
168	 * has always been each caller's own responsibility (see the Recently-Viewed branch below), and
169	 * this is the one piece of copy this container itself needs.
170	 */
171	const messages = defineMessages({
172	  seeFullHistory: {
173	    id: 'recommended_products.link.see_full_history',
174	    defaultMessage: 'See Full History',
175	  },
176	});
177	
178	/**
179	 * The one field this file reads off a recommendation-context product. A real
180	 * commerce-sdk-isomorphic Product shape underlies it, but @salesforce/retail-react-app's
181	 * useEinstein/ProductScroller ship untyped (vendor.d.ts's wildcard), so this is narrowed
182	 * to exactly the field touched here rather than invented more broadly (AGENTS.md > Type
183	 * Definitions: hand-roll only the genuinely unexported shape actually used).
184	 */
185	type RecommendedProduct = { productId?: string };
186	
187	export type RecommendedProductsProps = {
188	  /* The title to appear above the product scroller */
189	  title?: ReactNode;
190	
191	  /* The zone to request */
192	  zone?: string;
193	
194	  /* The recommender to request */
195	  recommender?: string;
196	
197	  /* The products to use for recommendation context */
198	  products?: readonly Record<string, unknown>[];
199	
200	  /* Callback to determine if the component should fetch results */
201	  shouldFetch?: () => boolean;
202	
203	  // Index signature for the `...props` passthrough to ProductScroller (itself untyped — see
204	  // vendor.d.ts). Without it, the destructured rest types as `{}` instead of accepting arbitrary
205	  // passthrough, which is the base file's actual intent: forwarding whatever else the caller
206	  // passes.
207	  [key: string]: unknown;
208	};
209	
210	/**
211	 * A component for fetching and rendering product recommendations from the Einstein API
212	 * by a zone or a recommender name.
213	 */
214	const RecommendedProducts = ({
215	  zone,
216	  recommender,
217	  products,
218	  title,
219	  shouldFetch,
220	  ...props
221	}: RecommendedProductsProps) => {
222	  const { isLoading, recommendations, getZoneRecommendations, getRecommendations, sendClickReco, sendViewReco } =
223	    useEinstein();
224	  const { data: customer } = useCurrentCustomer();
225	  const { customerId } = customer;
226	  const { data: wishlist } = useWishList();
227	  const dataCloud = useDataCloud();
228	
229	  const createCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('createCustomerProductListItem');
230	  const deleteCustomerProductListItem = useShopperCustomersMutation('deleteCustomerProductListItem');
231	  const toast = useToast();
232	  const navigate = useNavigation();
233	  const intl = useIntl();
234	  // Same split product-list/productListCardMapper.ts's own consumer uses
235	  // (product-list/index.tsx): passed into the mapper rather than formatted there, keeping that
236	  // mapper free of any react-intl dependency of its own.
237	  const formatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => intl.formatNumber(amount, { style: 'currency', currency });
238	
239	  const ref = useRef();
240	  const isOnScreen = useIntersectionObserver(ref, { useOnce: true });
241	  const [_products, setProducts] = useState(products);
242	  // Cart-exclusion check (2026-09-10, Marcel: "no recently viewed on cart" — a standing product
243	  // decision, not an Einstein-not-deployed-yet placeholder). Cart has no Zimmermann override
244	  // (no overrides/app/pages/cart/ at all) — its base page imports this same overridden component
245	  // and passes `recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED}`, which resolves to the
246	  // exact same string as PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED (confirmed identical,
247	  // node_modules/.../constants.js:154-160), so the recommender check below cannot tell the two
248	  // apart by value alone. `.endsWith('/cart')`, not an exact match — AGENTS.md's Multi-site
249	  // section: a real storefront path is locale/site-prefixed (e.g. `/en-GB/cart`), so an exact
250	  // `=== '/cart'` would only ever match the default site.
251	  const location = useLocation();
252	  const isCartPage = location.pathname.endsWith('/cart');
253	  // The See-Full-History trigger threshold, resolved for whichever breakpoint is actually
254	  // current. Also unconditional per rules of hooks; only meaningful inside the Recently-Viewed
255	  // branch below, same as `useLocation()` immediately above (whose derived `isCartPage` is also
256	  // only meaningful there). Reads the current breakpoint only — no ResizeObserver, no runtime DOM
257	  // measurement, matching the AC's own viewport-relative "exceeds the visible rail width" wording
258	  // (Open Question 1). See the module docblock's own "See-Full-History link" section for why this
259	  // is no longer a plain `useBreakpointValue` call.
260	  const visibleCardCount = useRecentlyViewedRailVisibleCount();
261	  // `buildUrl` site/locale-prefixes an internal path (e.g. `/en-GB/recently-viewed` on a non-AU
262	  // storefront) — AGENTS.md's Multi-site section: never assume routing. The rail itself must not
263	  // build this prefix; this container does it once, here.
264	  const { buildUrl } = useMultiSite();
265	
266	  useEffect(() => {
267	    // Check if the component should fetch results or not. This is useful
268	    // when you are still waiting on additional data, like `products`.
269	    if (typeof shouldFetch === 'function' && !shouldFetch()) {
270	      return;
271	    }
272	
273	    // Fetch either zone or recommender, but not both. If a zone and recommender
274	    // name are both provided, `zone` takes precendence.
275	    if (zone) {
276	      getZoneRecommendations(zone, _products);
277	      return;
278	    }
279	    if (recommender) {
280	      getRecommendations(recommender, _products);
281	      return;
282	    }
283	  }, [zone, recommender, _products]);
284	
285	  useEffect(() => {
286	    // This is an optimization that eliminates superfluous rerenders/fetching by
287	    // keeping a copy of the `products` array prop in state for shallow comparison.
288	    if (!Array.isArray(products)) {
289	      return;
290	    }
291	    if (products.length !== _products?.length || !products.every((val, index) => val === _products?.[index])) {
292	      setProducts(products);
293	    }
294	  }, [products]);
295	
296	  useEffect(() => {
297	    if (isOnScreen && recommendations?.recs) {
298	      sendViewReco(
299	        {
300	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
301	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
302	        },
303	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
304	      );
305	      dataCloud.sendViewRecommendations(
306	        {
307	          recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
308	          __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
309	        },
310	        recommendations.recs.map((rec: { id?: string }) => ({ id: rec.id })),
311	      );
312	    }
313	  }, [isOnScreen, recommendations]);
314	
315	  // SFCC-83 — Recently Viewed only. Every other recommender falls through to the unchanged
316	  // ProductScroller branch below. This branch sits ahead of the base dead-check below (see this
317	  // file's own module docblock, point 3, for why that no longer strictly matters but is kept
318	  // anyway) — every path inside this `if` returns on its own, so it never falls through to that
319	  // dead-check or the ProductScroller return regardless. Every other recommender is unaffected:
320	  // they still hit the exact same dead-check + ProductScroller path below, unchanged, just after
321	  // this check now short-circuits past them when it applies.
322	  if (recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED) {
323	    // Cart exclusion (2026-09-10, Marcel) — see the isCartPage constant's own comment above for
324	    // why this can't be expressed as a distinct recommender value. No rail, no title, no
325	    // placeholder — same treatment as the empty-state gate below, just for a different reason.
326	    if (isCartPage) {
327	      return null;
328	    }
329	
330	    // AC 8's empty-state gate, now against Einstein's own recs directly (build plan step E1) —
331	    // see this file's own module docblock for why this one check covers both the loading case
332	    // (`recs` undefined until `getRecommendations` resolves) and the true zero-history case. No
333	    // rail, no title, no placeholder.
334	    if (!recommendations?.recs?.length) {
335	      return null;
336	    }
337	
338	    // `recommendations.recs` is `useEinstein()`'s own untyped (`any`) result — like the
339	    // `.find`/`.some`/`.map` callbacks elsewhere in this file that already read off it, the
340	    // mapping callback below needs an explicit parameter-type annotation to satisfy
341	    // `noImplicitAny`. `RecentlyViewedProduct` (recentlyViewedCard.ts's own alias for
342	    // `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`) is reused here rather than a hand-rolled inline shape, since
343	    // it already names every field `selectRecentlyViewedCard` reads, and this input is a strict
344	    // superset of it (see the module docblock above).
345	    const cards: ZimmProductCardProps[] = recommendations.recs
346	      .map((product: RecentlyViewedProduct) => selectRecentlyViewedCard(product, formatPrice))
347	      .filter((card: RecentlyViewedCard | null): card is RecentlyViewedCard => card !== null)
348	      .map(
349	        (card: RecentlyViewedCard): ZimmProductCardProps => ({
350	          ...card,
351	          // Inert for this variation — ZimmProductCardContent never mounts when
352	          // variation: 'recentlyViewed' (zimmProductCard/index.tsx's
353	          // VARIATION_CONFIG.showContent). 'h3' matches the one other established value for
354	          // this same required field (product-list/productListCardMapper.ts).
355	          headingLevel: 'h3',
356	          variation: 'recentlyViewed',
357	        }),
358	      );
359	
360	    // The See-Full-History link, finally wired in (was a stated "not yet built" gap on every
361	    // caller until now). Triggers when the shopper has more recently-viewed products
362	    // than fit in view at the *current* breakpoint — matching the AC's own "exceeds the visible
363	    // rail width" wording, which is viewport-relative, not a flat count. Compared against
364	    // `cards.length` (the full, unsliced count this container just built — up to
365	    // RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED, 24), not the rail's own internal 5-item render slice,
366	    // since the question is "does more exist than is visible", not "did we cap the render".
367	    const showSeeAllLink = cards.length > visibleCardCount;
368	
369	    return (
370	      // Ref-attachment point — see the module docblock's own isOnScreen/forwardRef note above for
371	      // why this wrapper exists at all. `{...props}` forwards the caller's own layout props (e.g.
372	      // PDP's `mx={{base: -4, md: -8, lg: 0}}`, Cart's `mx={{base: -4, sm: -6, lg: 0}}`) exactly
373	      // as the ProductScroller branch below already does — without it, this branch would render
374	      // inset inside the page's normal content padding while every sibling rail on the same page
375	      // bleeds edge-to-edge, and zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's own card-width math (e.g.
376	      // 201x2=402) assumes the full viewport width is actually available. `title` is passed
377	      // straight through with no `recommendations?.displayMessage` fallback — this component owns
378	      // no copy of its own for this branch (build plan A5/A6): the real title always comes from
379	      // the caller, regardless of whether Einstein's own `displayMessage` is present.
380	      <Box ref={ref} {...(props as BoxProps)}>
381	        <ZimmRecentlyViewedRail
382	          title={title}
383	          cards={cards}
384	          seeAllHref={showSeeAllLink ? buildUrl(RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE) : undefined}
385	          seeAllLabel={showSeeAllLink ? intl.formatMessage(messages.seeFullHistory) : undefined}
386	        />
387	      </Box>
388	    );
389	  }
390	
391	  // The component should remove itself altogether if it has no recommendations
392	  // and we aren't loading any.
393	  if (!isLoading && (!recommendations || recommendations.length < 1)) {
394	    return null;
395	  }
396	
397	  // TODO: DRY this handler when intl provider is available globally
398	  const addItemToWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
399	    try {
400	      if (!wishlist || !customerId) {
401	        return;
402	      }
403	      await createCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
404	        parameters: {
405	          listId: wishlist.id,
406	          customerId,
407	        },
408	        body: {
409	          quantity: 1,
410	          productId: product.productId,
411	          public: false,
412	          priority: 1,
413	          type: 'product',
414	        },
415	      });
416	
417	      toast({
418	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_ADDED_TO_WISHLIST, { quantity: 1 }),
419	        status: 'success',
420	        action: (
421	          // it would be better if we could use <Button as={Link}>
422	          // but unfortunately the Link component is not compatible
423	          // with Chakra Toast, since the ToastManager is rendered via portal
424	          // and the toast doesn't have access to intl provider, which is a
425	          // requirement of the Link component.
426	          <Button variant="link" onClick={() => navigate('/account/wishlist')}>
427	            {intl.formatMessage(TOAST_ACTION_VIEW_WISHLIST)}
428	          </Button>
429	        ),
430	      });
431	    } catch {
432	      toast({
433	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
434	        status: 'error',
435	      });
436	    }
437	  };
438	
439	  const removeItemFromWishlist = async (product: RecommendedProduct) => {
440	    try {
441	      const wishlistItem = wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.find(
442	        (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product.productId,
443	      );
444	      if (!wishlistItem || !wishlist || !customerId) {
445	        return;
446	      }
447	      await deleteCustomerProductListItem.mutateAsync({
448	        parameters: {
449	          customerId,
450	          itemId: wishlistItem.id,
451	          listId: wishlist.id,
452	        },
453	      });
454	      toast({
455	        title: intl.formatMessage(TOAST_MESSAGE_REMOVED_FROM_WISHLIST),
456	        status: 'success',
457	        id: product.productId,
458	      });
459	    } catch {
460	      toast({
461	        title: intl.formatMessage(API_ERROR_MESSAGE),
462	        status: 'error',
463	      });
464	    }
465	  };
466	
467	  return (
468	    <ProductScroller
469	      ref={ref}
470	      title={title || recommendations?.displayMessage}
471	      products={recommendations.recs}
472	      isLoading={isLoading}
473	      productTileProps={(product: RecommendedProduct) => ({
474	        onClick: () => {
475	          sendClickReco(
476	            {
477	              recommenderName: recommendations.recommenderName,
478	              __recoUUID: recommendations.recoUUID,
479	            },
480	            product,
481	          );
482	        },
483	        enableFavourite: true,
484	        isFavourite: wishlist?.customerProductListItems?.some(
485	          (item: { productId?: string }) => item.productId === product?.productId,
486	        ),
487	        onFavouriteToggle: (toBeFavourite: boolean) => {
488	          const action = toBeFavourite ? addItemToWishlist : removeItemFromWishlist;
489	          return action(product);
490	        },
491	      })}
492	      {...props}
493	    />
494	  );
495	};
496	
497	export default RecommendedProducts;

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * Maps one Recently Viewed product to the FULL `ZimmProductCard` props Recently Viewed's Full
3	 * History page (SFCC-84) renders — badge, size chips, was/now pricing and a multi-image gallery,
4	 * i.e. the `plp` variation's already-shipped shape, not `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s narrower
5	 * image-only rail shape (SFCC-83's `recentlyViewed` variation). Both mappers read the same
6	 * underlying input — a plain Commerce API `Product` from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
7	 * `getProducts` call — but produce deliberately different output shapes for two deliberately
8	 * different surfaces; see that mapper's own docblock for the rail's narrower contract and why it
9	 * stops at image-only.
10	 *
11	 * Added per the build plan's B2 discussion (finding 41b): "reuse the rail's mapper" was the
12	 * original, incorrect assumption for this page — `recentlyViewedCard.ts` cannot produce this
13	 * shape by its own design (image-only, no price, no gallery), so a second, separate mapper is
14	 * required. Per Jasmijn's SFCC-84 comment, the Full History card's default state is "image, name,
15	 * badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon" — exactly the `plp` variation's shape, which is why
16	 * this mapper's output includes `headingLevel: 'h3'` and `variation: 'plp'` directly (unlike
17	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s `RecentlyViewedCard`, which deliberately excludes both as its rail
18	 * container's job) — mirroring `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult`, which
19	 * bakes in the same two fields for the same reason: its output is meant to be spread straight
20	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` with nothing left for a caller to add.
21	 *
22	 * Modelled on `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s general style/docblock conventions (no React/react-intl
23	 * import, `formatPrice` injected as a parameter, same hard `null`-gate contract for a product
24	 * with no usable name/image) and on `overrides/app/pages/product-list/productListCardMapper.ts`
25	 * (the closest existing precedent producing this exact `plp`-variation output shape from a real
26	 * product). Ported, not imported, from both — a genuinely separate, self-contained module with
27	 * its own local type aliases, the same relationship `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already has to
28	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` (see that file's own docblock).
29	 *
30	 * **What's ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`, and what changed:**
31	 * `selectSizeChipValues` is re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly (the plain
32	 * `Product` shape) in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying
33	 * `VariationAttribute` shape is the same `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` type either way, so the
34	 * picking/mapping logic itself needed no change, only the input type.
35	 *
36	 * **Image resolution — revised 2026-09-09 to close the same real bug already fixed on
37	 * `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedCard.ts`: a colour-blind image pick, and API array
38	 * order trusted over the image filename's own sequence number.** `selectGalleryImages` used to
39	 * pick "whichever image group has the most images," viewtype-agnostic — actually a worse version
40	 * of the same bug: no colour scoping meant a multi-colour product's gallery could mix different
41	 * colours' photos, and no viewtype restriction meant it could pick a non-`medium` group (an
42	 * oversized image at thumbnail size, against AGENTS.md's image-sizing rule). Now shares one
43	 * `selectColourScopedImages` resolution — colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` first (colour from
44	 * `resolveViewedColour`, which is only ever the fallback half of `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
45	 * `resolveRepresentativeColour`: this input has no `representedProduct` field, see that function's
46	 * own doc), falling back to a viewtype-only match for a genuinely single-colour product whose one
47	 * group carries no colour tag at all, then sorted by the image filename's own sequence number
48	 * (same real defect: a colour-tagged group can come back `[2, 1, ...]`, not ascending). This one
49	 * array now feeds `primaryImage`, `primaryImageFallbacks`, `hoverImage` and `images` — mirroring
50	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectProductListCard` exactly, except `primaryImage` is the
51	 * array's own first entry rather than a separately-sourced `hit.image` (a plain `getProducts`
52	 * `Product` has no equivalent flat `image` field — a Search-hit-only convenience field) — the same
53	 * adaptation `recentlyViewedCard.ts` already made for its own single-image case.
54	 *
55	 * **Price handling is deliberately NOT copied from `productListCardMapper.ts`.** That mapper reads
56	 * the flat `hit.price` field for `currentPrice` while leaving `originalPrice` unset entirely — had
57	 * it called `getPriceData(hit).listPrice` for `originalPrice` while keeping `hit.price` for
58	 * `currentPrice`, the two would risk disagreeing on a multi-variant product, since `getPriceData`
59	 * internally sources its own `currentPrice` from `findLowestPrice()`, not from a flat `price`
60	 * field. Both `currentPrice` and `originalPrice` here come from one `getPriceData(product)` call
61	 * (base SFCC, `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils.js:123-170`,
62	 * confirmed by reading it directly) so the two halves can never disagree. `originalPrice` is only
63	 * ever set when that same call's `isOnSale` is `true` — a not-on-sale product must not render a
64	 * crossed-out price identical to its current one.
65	 *
66	 * **Badge — confirmed live, 2026-09-09, closing what was a real, stated gap.** Previously left
67	 * `undefined`: `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` has no typed `c_productBadges` field, and it was
68	 * unconfirmed whether the `getProducts` hydration endpoint populates this custom attribute at all
69	 * (as opposed to the search-index endpoint `productListCardMapper.ts` reads it from). Checked
70	 * directly against a real badged product (`4673TS251`) via a live PDP fetch (which reads the same
71	 * `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` shape `getProducts` does — `product-detail/index.tsx`'s own
72	 * `useProduct` call): the field is genuinely present — `c_productBadges: [{productBadge: 'Runway',
73	 * productBadgeUrl: '/category/runway'}, {productBadge: 'Exclusive', productBadgeUrl:
74	 * '/category/exclusive'}]` — confirming the hydration endpoint does carry it, at least for this
75	 * product. Interestingly, the *same* product's Search hit carried no `c_productBadges` at all at
76	 * the same moment — most likely the search index simply hadn't caught up yet with a recently-added
77	 * badge (SFCC search indexes rebuild on their own schedule, separate from live product/master data
78	 * reads), not a real difference in what each endpoint is capable of returning — but that's a
79	 * hypothesis, not independently re-verified here.
80	 *
81	 * `productBadgeUrl` is a real field on the live data above, discovered by this check — not
82	 * consumed here or anywhere in this codebase today. `badge` stays a plain label string (matching
83	 * `ZimmProductCardBaseProps.badge?: string`, and `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own read of the same
84	 * shape) — turning a badge into a link is a real, undesigned UI decision, not something to invent
85	 * silently here.
86	 */
87	import type { ShopperProductsTypes } from 'commerce-sdk-isomorphic';
88	import { getPriceData, filterImageGroups } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/product-utils';
89	import { productUrlBuilder } from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/url';
90	import type {
91	  ZimmProductCardBaseProps,
92	  ZimmProductCardPlpVariation,
93	  ZimmProductCardImage,
94	} from '../components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard';
95	import type { ZimmSizeChipValue } from '../components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmSizeChipGroup';
96	import {
97	  sortImagesBySequence,
98	  resolveFallbackColour,
99	  toGalleryAlt,
100	  resolveRequiredAlt,
101	} from './productCardMappingHelpers';
102	
103	/**
104	 * The real Commerce API `Product` this mapper reads — the same `ShopperProductsTypes.Product`
105	 * `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` produces and `recentlyViewedCard.ts` also consumes, augmented
106	 * with `c_productBadges` — same narrow-augmentation pattern as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
107	 * `ProductListSearchHit`, and the same reasoning: the SDK's own `Product` type has no field for
108	 * this custom attribute, only a generic `{[key: string]: any}` index signature, so this documents
109	 * the real, confirmed-live shape (see this module's own docblock's "Badge" section) rather than
110	 * reading through `any`. Not otherwise an augmentation — everything else this mapper reads is
111	 * already typed by the SDK — so this stays close to "a plain alias" in spirit, just no longer
112	 * literally one.
113	 */
114	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct = ShopperProductsTypes.Product & {
115	  // productBadgeUrl is real, confirmed-live data (see this module's own docblock's "Badge"
116	  // section) but genuinely unused below -- typed anyway so a test fixture built from the real
117	  // wire shape doesn't have to omit it to satisfy this type.
118	  c_productBadges?: Array<{ productBadge?: string; productBadgeUrl?: string }>;
119	};
120	
121	/** Formats a bare amount for the storefront. Injected so this module stays free of react-intl —
122	 *  same shape as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `FormatPrice`, redeclared locally for the same
123	 *  separate-module reason as `RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct` above. */
124	export type FormatPrice = (amount: number, currency: string) => string;
125	
126	/**
127	 * The full `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard` props this mapper produces — badge, size chips,
128	 * was/now pricing, multi-image gallery, heading level and variation all included. Mirrors
129	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` (unexported from that file, so
130	 * redeclared here rather than imported) — this mapper's output is meant to be spread straight
131	 * into `<ZimmProductCard>` by its page container (SFCC-84's Full History page, not yet built)
132	 * with nothing left to add, the same convenience that shape already gives PLP's own page.
133	 */
134	export type RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = ZimmProductCardBaseProps & ZimmProductCardPlpVariation;
135	
136	/** The correctly-sized product image view for the required `primaryImage` slot — same constant,
137	 *  same reasoning, as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE`: never serve an
138	 *  arbitrary-sized image at thumbnail size (AGENTS.md's image-sizing guidance). */
139	const MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE = 'medium';
140	
141	/** The variation-attribute id this mapper reads for size chips — named per conventions.md's
142	 *  no-magic-strings rule. `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectSizeChipValues`, which this is
143	 *  ported from, uses the literal inline; named here instead since this is a fresh file. */
144	const SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'size';
145	
146	/** The variation-attribute id `filterImageGroups` matches an image group's colour against — same
147	 *  constant, same reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own. */
148	const COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID = 'color';
149	
150	/**
151	 * Resolves which real colour this product's images should come from — now the shared
152	 * `resolveFallbackColour` (`productCardMappingHelpers.ts`) directly, same as
153	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s identical `resolveViewedColour`: there is no `representedProduct`
154	 * branch to add here, since this input is a plain `ShopperProductsTypes.Product` (from
155	 * `getProducts`), which has no such field at all (confirmed against the SDK's own type).
156	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveRepresentativeColour` layers exactly one extra branch
157	 * (a `representedProduct` match, Search-hit-only) in front of this same shared fallback. Returns
158	 * `undefined` when there are no variants at all — `selectColourScopedImages` below then falls back
159	 * to an unscoped, viewtype-only lookup, never a throw.
160	 */
161	const resolveViewedColour = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): string | undefined =>
162	  resolveFallbackColour(product.variants, COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
163	
164	/**
165	 * Sorts by the merchandiser-assigned sequence number baked into each image's own filename
166	 * (e.g. `.../images/1.4673ts251.gvscp.guava-seascape.jpg` → `1`) — confirmed live on `4673TS251`,
167	 * whose colour-tagged medium group came back `[2, 1, 3, ...]`.
168	 *
169	 * Shared with `productListCardMapper.ts` and `recentlyViewedCard.ts` — see
170	 * `productCardMappingHelpers.ts`'s own docblock for why a shared primitive rather than three
171	 * separate copies (all three had drifted onto the identical non-transitive-comparator bug,
172	 * CodeRabbit 2026-09-10).
173	 */
174	const sortByImageSequence = (images: ZimmProductCardImage[]): ZimmProductCardImage[] =>
175	  sortImagesBySequence(images, (image) => image.src);
176	
177	/**
178	 * `getPriceData`'s own return shape (base SFCC, `product-utils.js:123-170`, confirmed by reading
179	 * it directly), narrowed to the three fields this mapper reads. `@salesforce/retail-react-app`
180	 * ships no TypeScript types — this subpath falls through `overrides/app/types/vendor.d.ts`'s
181	 * catch-all `declare module '@salesforce/retail-react-app/*'`, a shorthand ambient module
182	 * declaration that types the whole module `any`, so `getPriceData`'s real return is implicitly
183	 * `any`. Declaring a local, narrow type for the fields actually read — rather than letting that
184	 * `any` propagate into this module's own types — matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
185	 * narrow-local-type pattern for the same untyped function (typescript.md's no-`any` rule). This
186	 * is a type annotation documenting an assumed shape, not a runtime guarantee: TypeScript allows
187	 * assigning `any` to any narrower type with no check, so the real correctness proof is the test
188	 * file's own direct comparison against a real `getPriceData` call, not this annotation alone.
189	 */
190	type SfccPriceData = {
191	  /** `findLowestPrice()`'s own `minPrice` — never `product.price` directly. This is the field
192	   *  `productListCardMapper.ts` does not use for its own `currentPrice` (it reads the flat
193	   *  `hit.price` field instead) — see this module's own docblock for why that risks disagreeing
194	   *  with a `getPriceData`-derived `originalPrice` on a multi-variant product. */
195	  currentPrice: number;
196	  /** The highest tiered price found — "was" price. `undefined` when the product has no
197	   *  `tieredPrices` at all (there is then no maximum to compute). */
198	  listPrice: number | undefined;
199	  /** `currentPrice < listPrice` — always `false`, never `true`, when `listPrice` is `undefined`
200	   *  (a numeric comparison against `undefined` evaluates to `false` in JS, never throws). */
201	  isOnSale: boolean;
202	};
203	
204	/** The real `imageGroups[].images[]` element shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic`'s own
205	 *  `ShopperProductsTypes.Image`) — named `RawImage` to match `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
206	 *  local name for the equivalent concept, but pointed at the real SDK type rather than that
207	 *  file's hand-rolled shape (AGENTS.md > Type Definitions: don't re-declare a type the SDK
208	 *  already exports). */
209	type RawImage = ShopperProductsTypes.Image;
210	
211	const toCardImage = (image: RawImage | undefined): ZimmProductCardImage | undefined => {
212	  const src = image?.disBaseLink ?? image?.link;
213	  if (!src) return undefined;
214	  return { src, alt: toGalleryAlt(image?.alt) };
215	};
216	
217	/**
218	 * The colour + `medium`-viewtype-scoped image list this product's card uses — one lookup feeding
219	 * four separate things below (`primaryImage`, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the
220	 * broken-image fallback candidates), so none of them can ever disagree with each other or with the
221	 * resolved colour. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
222	 * `selectColourScopedImages`, re-pointed at `product.imageGroups` (the plain `getProducts` shape)
223	 * in place of a `ProductSearchHit`'s own same-named field — the underlying `ImageGroup`/`Image`
224	 * types are identical either way (confirmed directly against
225	 * `node_modules/commerce-sdk-isomorphic/lib/index.esm.d.ts`).
226	 *
227	 * **Two-pass, not one** — same real bug as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own version closes: a
228	 * strict colour-scoped `filterImageGroups` match requires the group to explicitly declare a
229	 * matching `variationAttributes` entry, but a single-colour product's medium group commonly
230	 * carries no `variationAttributes` at all (nothing to disambiguate), which would make a
231	 * colour-scoped-only lookup exclude the group and return nothing. Falls back to a viewtype-only
232	 * match in that case. Never the reverse — a real colour-scoped match never falls back further, to
233	 * avoid re-mixing colours.
234	 */
235	const selectColourScopedImages = (
236	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
237	  colour: string | undefined,
238	): ZimmProductCardImage[] => {
239	  const colourScopedGroups = colour
240	    ? (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
241	        viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
242	        variationValues: { [COLOUR_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID]: colour },
243	      }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[])
244	    : [];
245	
246	  const groups =
247	    colourScopedGroups.length > 0
248	      ? colourScopedGroups
249	      : (filterImageGroups(product.imageGroups ?? [], {
250	          viewType: MEDIUM_VIEW_TYPE,
251	        }) as ShopperProductsTypes.ImageGroup[]);
252	
253	  const images = (groups[0]?.images ?? [])
254	    .map(toCardImage)
255	    .filter((image): image is ZimmProductCardImage => Boolean(image));
256	
257	  return sortByImageSequence(images);
258	};
259	
260	/**
261	 * Picks this product's gallery from the colour-scoped image list above — matches
262	 * `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s own "no gallery" contract for 0 or 1 images (returns `undefined`, never
263	 * a 1-length array). Kept exported and independently tested, same as
264	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` — `selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard`
265	 * below calls `selectColourScopedImages` directly instead (one shared computation feeding
266	 * `primaryImage`/`primaryImageFallbacks`/`hoverImage`/`images` at once), matching that file's own
267	 * documented, deliberate minor redundancy rather than introducing a new one.
268	 */
269	export const selectGalleryImages = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmProductCardImage[] | undefined => {
270	  const images = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
271	  return images.length > 1 ? images : undefined;
272	};
273	
274	/**
275	 * Reads the "size" variation attribute (if this product has one) into the shape
276	 * `ZimmSizeChipGroup` expects. Ported near-verbatim from `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own
277	 * `selectSizeChipValues`, re-pointed at `product.variationAttributes` directly — `orderable` on
278	 * each value already reflects real stock for that specific size, so it maps directly to
279	 * `isDisabled` with no extra lookup needed.
280	 */
281	export const selectSizeChipValues = (product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct): ZimmSizeChipValue[] => {
282	  const sizeAttribute = product.variationAttributes?.find((attr) => attr.id === SIZE_VARIATION_ATTRIBUTE_ID);
283	  return (sizeAttribute?.values ?? []).map((value) => ({
284	    value: value.value,
285	    label: value.name ?? value.value,
286	    isDisabled: value.orderable === false,
287	  }));
288	};
289	
290	/** What `resolveOrderableVariant` resolves a selected size chip value to — same shape, same
291	 *  reasoning, as `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ResolvedVariant`: the real, orderable SKU for
292	 *  that specific size, not the master id this product otherwise defaults to. */
293	export type ResolvedVariant = {
294	  productId: string;
295	  price: number | undefined;
296	  orderable: boolean;
297	};
298	
299	/**
300	 * Resolves a selected size CHIP VALUE to its real orderable variant — ported near-verbatim from
301	 * `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `resolveOrderableVariant`, re-pointed at this input's own
302	 * `variants` field (identical shape either way — both are `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` `Variant`
303	 * types). Returns `null` when there is no matching variant at all — callers fall back to this
304	 * product's own default id/price in that case, the same default that already existed before
305	 * size-aware Add to Bag was ever selectable.
306	 */
307	export const resolveOrderableVariant = (
308	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
309	  sizeValue: string,
310	): ResolvedVariant | null => {
311	  const variant = product.variants?.find((candidate) => candidate.variationValues?.size === sizeValue);
312	  if (!variant) return null;
313	
314	  return {
315	    productId: variant.productId,
316	    price: variant.price,
317	    orderable: variant.orderable !== false,
318	  };
319	};
320	
321	/**
322	 * Derives `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` from a single `getPriceData(product)` call — see this
323	 * module's own docblock for why both must come from the same call rather than mixing a flat
324	 * `product.price` field for one and `getPriceData` for the other. No `opts` passed — the default
325	 * `quantity: 1` is correct for a single-unit card display (matches `variantScopedPrice.ts`'s own
326	 * no-opts calls for the same reason). No hardcoded fallback currency — if either the price or the
327	 * currency is absent, formatting is skipped rather than guessed, matching `productInfo.ts`'s and
328	 * `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own "no hardcoded fallback currency" rule.
329	 */
330	const selectPriceFields = (
331	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct,
332	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
333	): Pick<RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard, 'currentPrice' | 'originalPrice'> => {
334	  const priceData: SfccPriceData = getPriceData(product);
335	
336	  const currentPrice =
337	    typeof priceData.currentPrice === 'number' && product.currency
338	      ? formatPrice(priceData.currentPrice, product.currency)
339	      : undefined;
340	
341	  // Only set when isOnSale is true -- a not-on-sale product must not render a crossed-out price
342	  // identical to its current one.
343	  const originalPrice =
344	    priceData.isOnSale && typeof priceData.listPrice === 'number' && product.currency
345	      ? formatPrice(priceData.listPrice, product.currency)
346	      : undefined;
347	
348	  return { currentPrice, originalPrice };
349	};
350	
351	/**
352	 * @param product - A plain Commerce API product from `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts`'s own
353	 *   `getProducts` call, or `undefined`/`null` while that data is not yet available.
354	 * @param formatPrice - Currency formatter, normally `intl.formatNumber`.
355	 * @returns Props for the `plp`-variation `ZimmProductCard`, or `null` when the product has no
356	 *   usable name or no usable image — never a broken card, never a throw. Same hard-gate contract
357	 *   as `recentlyViewedCard.ts`'s own `selectRecentlyViewedCard`. `onAddToBag`/`selectedSizeChipValue`/
358	 *   `onSizeChipSelect` are deliberately not populated here — same split
359	 *   `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `ProductListCardResult` documents: this mapper is a pure data
360	 *   function with no per-card selection state of its own, so the page container wires those three
361	 *   (see `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx`'s own per-card size-chip state).
362	 */
363	export const selectRecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard = (
364	  product: RecentlyViewedFullHistoryProduct | undefined | null,
365	  formatPrice: FormatPrice,
366	): RecentlyViewedFullHistoryCard | null => {
367	  if (!product?.name) return null;
368	
369	  // One resolution feeds primaryImage, the gallery, the hover-swap image, and the broken-image
370	  // fallback candidates below — see selectColourScopedImages's own docblock for why.
371	  const scopedImages = selectColourScopedImages(product, resolveViewedColour(product));
372	  const [firstImage] = scopedImages;
373	  if (!firstImage) return null;
374	
375	  // Required-non-empty alt for the primary position only — shared resolveRequiredAlt
376	  // (productCardMappingHelpers.ts, also used by recentlyViewedCard.ts's own primary image). Was
377	  // `firstImage.alt || product.name` here (no `.trim()`) until 2026-09-10, a real gap this shared
378	  // helper closes: a whitespace-only alt is a non-empty string, so it passed straight through
379	  // instead of falling back — confirmed with a real whitespace-only-alt repro. The rest of
380	  // scopedImages keeps toCardImage's plain alt (matching productListCardMapper.ts's own gallery
381	  // images, which get no such treatment either) since only the primary slot ever carried this
382	  // extra safeguard.
383	  const primaryImage: ZimmProductCardImage = { ...firstImage, alt: resolveRequiredAlt(firstImage.alt, product.name) };
384	
385	  const { currentPrice, originalPrice } = selectPriceFields(product, formatPrice);
386	
387	  return {
388	    id: product.id,
389	    href: productUrlBuilder({ id: product.id }),
390	    name: product.name,
391	    headingLevel: 'h3',
392	    primaryImage,
393	    // Ordered backup candidates if primaryImage itself fails to load — same real, live defect
394	    // productListCardMapper.ts's own primaryImageFallbacks closes.
395	    primaryImageFallbacks: scopedImages,
396	    // The second image in the same colour-scoped sequence — revealed on hover. undefined when
397	    // there is no second image, which ZimmProductCardMedia already treats as "no swap".
398	    hoverImage: scopedImages[1],
399	    images: scopedImages.length > 1 ? scopedImages : undefined,
400	    currentPrice,
401	    originalPrice,
402	    // product.master is this master product's own overall orderability (ShopperProductsTypes.Master
403	    // — confirmed via the SDK's own type) — the equivalent of productListCardMapper.ts's flat
404	    // hit.orderable for this input shape, which has no such flat field of its own.
405	    isUnavailable: product.master?.orderable === false,
406	    // Single highest-priority badge -- confirmed live, 2026-09-09 (see this module's own docblock's
407	    // "Badge" section). SFCC-225's own hook already sorts c_productBadges by badgePriorityOrder
408	    // before this ever reaches the frontend, matching productListCardMapper.ts's own identical read.
409	    badge: product.c_productBadges?.[0]?.productBadge,
410	    variation: 'plp',
411	    sizeChipValues: selectSizeChipValues(product),
412	  };
413	};

pattern already used by the other four recommenders on this same file (if the Einstein call
fails/errors, that path already degrades to no recommendations shown, not a broken page — confirmed
by reading the existing error handling in `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails` try/catch).

wiring Recently-Viewed through the same mechanism introduces no new consent-posture change; this
is a pre-existing, platform-wide gap outside this task's scope to fix.

### Acceptance criteria

Same ACs as the original SFCC-83/84 build (AC 2, 6, 7, 8 for the Rail; SFCC-84's own Full History
ACs) — unchanged by this task. The one behavioural difference worth naming explicitly: AC 7
(cross-device history restore on login) becomes genuinely achievable once Einstein is real
(server-side history, not device-local storage) — this was the interim mechanism's one stated,
accepted gap, and this branch is what actually closes it.
